comparison: Both strongly support the differential regeneration findings (C2, C13-C19, C72). OpenEval emphasizes converging evidence from multiple experimental approaches. Peer reviewers describe data quality as 'very good' and evidence as 'solid.' OpenEval also includes C73 which peer reviewers group with mechanistic speculation (R8). Peer reviewers additionally include C68-C70 (inverse relationship conclusions) which OpenEval evaluates separately (R9).

Both support the RNA-seq differential expression findings. OpenEval focuses on C3, C24, C28-C30 (DEG overlap and neuron-type-specific genes) with emphasis on methodological soundness. Peer reviewers address C3, C24, C31-C35 (including pathway enrichment), describing 'solid evidence' and 'comprehensive expression profiling.' OpenEval evaluates pathway enrichment claims (C31-C35) separately in R5.

Both support Med12 findings (C4, C43, C45-C47, C71). OpenEval emphasizes strong evidence through RNA-seq and functional validation with cell-type specificity. Peer reviewers acknowledge this as 'proof of concept' but note 'Further investigation is needed to define this responsiveness in detail.' Peer reviewers also include C74 (TGF-β mechanism hypothesis) which OpenEval evaluates as UNCERTAIN in R11.

Both support neurotrophin response findings (C39-C42, C78-C80). OpenEval provides detailed assessment of quantitative measurements and statistical significance. Peer reviewers implicitly accept these findings through acknowledgment of neurotrophin receptor signaling discussion. Peer reviewers also include C36-C38 (pan-neuronal measurements) which OpenEval evaluates separately in R10.

Both address pathway enrichment claims (C31-C35). OpenEval notes these are supported by KEGG/GO analysis but emphasizes functional significance is not experimentally validated, only inferred. Peer reviewers group these with broader differential expression findings (C3, C24) and describe evidence as 'solid' without distinguishing between direct experimental data and bioinformatic inference.

Perfect agreement on Ribotag validation (C20-C23). OpenEval describes validation as 'thorough and appropriate' with multiple complementary approaches. Peer reviewers describe the Ribotag approach positively and note 'quality of data presentation appears to be very good,' implicitly supporting the technical validation.

Perfect agreement on TRPV1-Cre characterization (C12). OpenEval supports the claim with immunofluorescence data but notes ~27% of population remains uncharacterized. Peer reviewers implicitly accept this characterization as part of overall methodology without explicit critique, suggesting acceptance of the mouse model validation.

Both support specific gene expression findings (C25-C27). OpenEval emphasizes RNA-seq data with immunohistochemical validation for p75NTR and ATF2. Peer reviewers implicitly accept these findings through acknowledgment of heterogeneous responses and discussion of guidance molecules. Peer reviewers also include C28-C30 which OpenEval evaluates with C3, C24 in R2.

Both support inverse relationship conclusions (C68-C70). OpenEval treats these as conclusions drawn from regeneration rate data, noting the motoneuron exception. Peer reviewers group these with primary regeneration findings (C2, C13-C19, C72) rather than evaluating them as separate interpretive claims.

Both support pan-neuronal neurite outgrowth findings (C36-C38). OpenEval notes statistical significance but highlights the small NT-3 effect size with high variability. Peer reviewers group these with cell-type-specific neurotrophin responses (C39-C42, C78-C80) without distinguishing the marginal effect size concern.

Both evaluate TGF-β mechanism hypothesis (C74) with caution. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting qPCR showed no significant changes in TGF-β pathway genes. Peer reviewers support Med12 findings but note 'Further investigation is needed,' acknowledging the mechanistic hypothesis requires validation.

Both evaluate mechanistic speculations (C75-C77) as uncertain/requiring validation. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting gene expression patterns are supported but causal relationships are not experimentally validated. Peer reviewers acknowledge 'multiple explanations' and state 'Further investigation is needed to define this responsiveness in detail.' Peer reviewers also include C73, C82.

Both address speculative claims (C81-C82). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting these are hypotheses not systematically tested. Peer reviewers group C82 with other mechanistic speculations (C73, C75-C77) and note need for further investigation. Peer reviewers also evaluate C81 separately in R10 as implicitly accepted speculation.

Partial overlap on C81. OpenEval evaluates C81-C82 together as UNCERTAIN speculations attempting to explain observed data. Peer reviewers treat C81 (and C1) as framing/speculative elements that are implicitly accepted without explicit critique, suggesting lower concern about these claims.

Both support literature review claims (C5-C11). OpenEval confirms these establish appropriate context with relevant citations. Peer reviewers implicitly accept these background claims as part of manuscript framing without explicit evaluation, focusing instead on novel experimental findings.

Both support extensive literature review claims (C44, C48-C67). OpenEval confirms appropriate citations providing context for RNA-seq interpretation and gene selection rationale. Peer reviewers implicitly accept these contextual claims, with their positive overall assessment suggesting acceptance of the literature framework.

Peer reviewers address C1 (general introductory statement) which OpenEval does not evaluate separately. Peer reviewers note implicit acceptance through lack of critique. This represents a framing claim that OpenEval may have considered too general to warrant specific evaluation.
